ex.zh: 放大鏡有一片凸透鏡。

ex.en: The convex mirror lets drivers see around the corner.
ex.zh: 凸面鏡讓駕駛能看到轉角另一邊。

ex.en: The shape on the left is a convex, while the other one has a dent.
ex.zh: 左邊的形狀是凸形，另一個則有凹陷。

ex.en: In geometry class, we learned to tell a convex from a concave.
ex.zh: 在幾何課上，我們學會分辨凸形與凹形。

ex.en: The team scored on a quick counterattack.
ex.zh: 球隊靠一次快速反擊得分。

ex.en: The company launched a counterattack against its rival's advertising.
ex.zh: 公司對競爭對手的廣告發動反擊。

ex.en: The army counterattacked at dawn.
ex.zh: 軍隊在黎明時發動反攻。

ex.en: When the other team ran forward, we counterattacked down the left side.
ex.zh: 對方隊伍壓上時，我們從左路反擊。

ex.en: We grilled corn on the cob at the picnic.
ex.zh: 我們在野餐時烤了玉米棒。

ex.en: He chewed the kernels off the cob.
ex.zh: 他把玉米粒從玉米棒上啃下來。

ex.en: The government conscripted young men into the army.
ex.zh: 政府徵召年輕男子入伍。

ex.en: He was conscripted at eighteen and served for two years.
ex.zh: 他十八歲被徵召入伍，服役兩年。

ex.en: Each conscript received a uniform and a bed in the barracks.
ex.zh: 每位新兵都領到一套制服和營房裡的一張床。

ex.en: The conscript wrote letters to his family every week.
ex.zh: 那名新兵每週都寫信給家人。

ex.en: The leaders issued a joint communique after the meeting.
ex.zh: 領導人在會議後發表了聯合公報。

ex.en: The communique said that talks would continue next week.
ex.zh: 公報指出會談將於下週繼續。

ex.en: Students can buy tickets at a concessionary price.
ex.zh: 學生可以用優惠價購票。

ex.en: The museum offers concessionary rates for seniors.
ex.zh: 博物館提供長者優惠票價。

ex.en: The condor spread its huge wings and rose above the mountains.
ex.zh: 神鷹展開巨大的翅膀，飛上群山之上。

ex.en: We saw a condor circling slowly over the canyon.
ex.zh: 我們看到一隻神鷹在峽谷上空緩緩盤旋。

ex.en: The court will decide on the constitutionality of the new law.
ex.zh: 法院將裁定這項新法是否合憲。

ex.en: Experts debated the constitutionality of the plan.
ex.zh: 專家們討論這項計畫是否符合憲法。

collapsing.zh: 倒塌；崩潰（collapse 的現在分詞）

ex.en: The old bridge is collapsing under the weight of the trucks.
ex.zh: 那座舊橋在卡車的重量下正在倒塌。

ex.en: He kept working until he was nearly collapsing from tiredness.
ex.zh: 他一直工作到累得快要昏倒。

ex.en: The councilman spoke at the meeting about the new road.
ex.zh: 這位市議員在會議上談到新道路。

ex.en: Local residents wrote to their councilman about the noise.
ex.zh: 當地居民寫信給市議員反映噪音問題。

ex.en: The child had a convulsion because of a high fever.
ex.zh: 孩子因為高燒而抽搐。

ex.en: The doctor explained what to do if someone has a convulsion.
ex.zh: 醫生說明了有人抽搐時該怎麼做。

ex.en: The country went through a political convulsion last year.
ex.zh: 這個國家去年經歷了一場政治動盪。

ex.en: The news caused a convulsion in the stock market.
ex.zh: 這則消息使股市劇烈震盪。

ex.en: The confiscation of the illegal goods happened at the border.
ex.zh: 非法物品在邊境被沒收了。

ex.en: Students faced confiscation of their phones during class.
ex.zh: 學生上課時手機有被沒收的風險。

ex.en: Cognac is a kind of brandy made in France.
ex.zh: 干邑是一種產於法國的白蘭地。

ex.en: He sipped a glass of cognac by the fire.
ex.zh: 他在爐火旁啜飲著一杯干邑。

corinthian.zh: （古希臘）科林斯的；科林斯式的

ex.en: The temple was built with tall Corinthian columns.
ex.zh: 這座神殿用高大的科林斯式柱子建成。

ex.en: Corinthian capitals are decorated with carved leaves.
ex.zh: 科林斯式柱頭飾有雕刻的葉子圖案。

ex.en: The church held a congregational meeting after the service.
ex.zh: 教會在禮拜後召開了會眾大會。

ex.en: Congregational singing filled the hall.
ex.zh: 全體會眾的歌聲響徹大廳。

courtly.zh: 彬彬有禮的；有宮廷風範的

ex.en: He bowed with courtly grace and kissed her hand.
ex.zh: 他以優雅的風度鞠躬並親吻她的手。

ex.en: The poem describes courtly love in medieval times.
ex.zh: 這首詩描寫中世紀的宮廷愛情。

ex.en: The corona of the sun can be seen during a total eclipse.
ex.zh: 日全食時可以看見太陽的日冕。

ex.en: A faint corona of light surrounded the streetlamp in the fog.
ex.zh: 霧中路燈周圍有一圈淡淡的光暈。

ex.en: A broken cog stopped the old clock from running.
ex.zh: 一個壞掉的輪齒讓老時鐘停了下來。

ex.en: Each cog in the machine turns the next one.
ex.zh: 機器裡的每個齒輪都帶動下一個。

ex.en: He felt like a small cog in a huge company.
ex.zh: 他覺得自己只是一家大公司裡的小齒輪。

ex.en: In the past, women often wore a corset under their dresses.
ex.zh: 過去女性常在洋裝裡面穿緊身胸衣。

ex.en: The museum displays a corset from the nineteenth century.
ex.zh: 博物館展出一件十九世紀的緊身胸衣。

ex.en: The thief and his confederate were caught outside the shop.
ex.zh: 小偷和他的同夥在店外被抓住了。

ex.en: She trusted him as a loyal confederate in the project.
ex.zh: 她把他當作計畫中忠實的盟友。

ex.en: The confederate states agreed to share a common defense.
ex.zh: 這些結盟的邦同意共同防衛。

ex.en: They formed a confederate group of small companies.
ex.zh: 他們組成了一個由小公司聯合起來的團體。

ex.en: The book looks at the colonisation of the island.
ex.zh: 這本書探討這座島嶼的殖民歷史。

ex.en: Colonisation changed the lives of local people.
ex.zh: 殖民改變了當地人民的生活。

ex.en: He fell off his bike and broke his collarbone.
ex.zh: 他從腳踏車上摔下來，摔斷了鎖骨。

ex.en: The doctor pressed gently on my collarbone.
ex.zh: 醫生輕輕按壓我的鎖骨。

ex.en: The Cossack rode a horse across the plain.
ex.zh: 那位哥薩克人騎馬穿越平原。

ex.en: The Cossacks are known as skilled horsemen.
ex.zh: 哥薩克人以精湛的騎術聞名。

ex.en: The gymnast can contort her body into amazing shapes.
ex.zh: 那位體操選手能把身體扭成驚人的形狀。

ex.en: Pain made his face contort.
ex.zh: 疼痛讓他的臉扭曲變形。

colombo.zh: 可倫坡（斯里蘭卡最大城市）

ex.en: Colombo is the largest city in Sri Lanka.
ex.zh: 可倫坡是斯里蘭卡最大的城市。

ex.en: Many flights land in Colombo every day.
ex.zh: 每天都有許多班機降落在可倫坡。

ex.en: I sliced a courgette and fried it with garlic.
ex.zh: 我把一條櫛瓜切片，和蒜頭一起煎。

ex.en: She grows courgettes in her small garden.
ex.zh: 她在小花園裡種了櫛瓜。

ex.en: The word "home" connotes warmth and safety.
ex.zh: 「家」這個字隱含著溫暖與安全。

ex.en: Red often connotes danger in traffic signs.
ex.zh: 在交通標誌中，紅色常暗示危險。

ex.en: Oxygen is a constitutive element of water.
ex.zh: 氧是水的組成元素。

ex.en: Trust is a constitutive part of any strong friendship.
ex.zh: 信任是任何深厚友誼的基本組成部分。

ex.en: The mechanic wore blue coveralls covered in oil.
ex.zh: 那位技師穿著沾滿機油的藍色連身工作服。

ex.en: Painters often put on coveralls to protect their clothes.
ex.zh: 油漆工常穿連身工作服來保護衣服。

ex.en: The heavy weight on the left counterbalances the load on the right.
ex.zh: 左邊的重物與右邊的負荷互相平衡。

ex.en: Her calm nature helps counterbalance his nervous energy.
ex.zh: 她沉穩的個性能平衡他的緊張急躁。

ex.en: Strong courts act as a counterbalance to government power.
ex.zh: 強而有力的法院能制衡政府權力。

ex.en: The crane has a heavy block as a counterbalance at the back.
ex.zh: 起重機後方有一塊重物作為平衡配重。

ex.en: The conformation of the protein decides how it works in the body.
ex.zh: 蛋白質的結構形態決定它在體內如何運作。

ex.en: Judges examine the conformation of each horse at the show.
ex.zh: 評審在展覽上檢查每匹馬的體型結構。

ex.en: He dresses conservatively in a dark suit and plain tie.
ex.zh: 他穿著保守，深色西裝配素色領帶。

ex.en: My grandfather invests his money very conservatively.
ex.zh: 我祖父投資非常保守。

ex.en: The repairs will cost at least $500, conservatively speaking.
ex.zh: 保守來說，修理至少要花五百美元。

ex.en: The company conservatively estimates a small profit this year.
ex.zh: 公司保守估計今年會有小額獲利。

corporatist.zh: 組合主義者；社團主義者

ex.en: The professor described him as a corporatist who favors cooperation between business and labor.
ex.zh: 教授形容他是主張勞資合作的組合主義者。

ex.en: A corporatist believes society works best when groups cooperate under the state.
ex.zh: 組合主義者認為，社會在各團體於國家之下合作時運作得最好。

ex.en: All new students attended the opening convocation at the university.
ex.zh: 所有新生都參加了大學的開學典禮。

ex.en: The principal gave a speech at the annual convocation.
ex.zh: 校長在年度大會上發表了演說。

ex.en: The convocation of the committee was announced last week.
ex.zh: 委員會的召集通知在上週發布了。

ex.en: Corporatism is an idea in which groups like business and labor work together with the state.
ex.zh: 組合主義是一種讓企業、勞工等團體與國家合作的思想。

ex.en: The history teacher explained how corporatism shaped some economies in the twentieth century.
ex.zh: 歷史老師說明了組合主義如何影響二十世紀的一些經濟體。

collapsed.zh: 倒塌；崩潰（collapse 的過去式）

ex.en: The old bridge collapsed during the storm.
ex.zh: 那座老橋在暴風雨中倒塌了。

ex.en: The company collapsed after losing its biggest customer.
ex.zh: 這家公司在失去最大客戶後倒閉了。

ex.en: The runner collapsed at the finish line.
ex.zh: 跑者在終點線昏倒了。

ex.en: He collapsed onto the sofa after a long day.
ex.zh: 漫長的一天後，他癱倒在沙發上。

ex.en: Rescuers searched the collapsed building for survivors.
ex.zh: 救難人員搜索倒塌的建築尋找生還者。

ex.en: A collapsed tent lay on the ground after the wind.
ex.zh: 風吹過後，一頂塌掉的帳篷躺在地上。

ex.en: We hired a conveyancer to handle the sale of our house.
ex.zh: 我們請了辦理產權轉讓的律師來處理房子的買賣。

ex.en: The conveyancer checked all the documents before we signed.
ex.zh: 在我們簽名前，這位產權轉讓律師查核了所有文件。

ex.en: The compositor set each line of type by hand.
ex.zh: 排字工人用手排好每一行鉛字。

ex.en: In the old days, a compositor worked at a print shop.
ex.zh: 在以前，排字工人在印刷廠工作。

ex.en: "Heavy rain" is a common collocation in English.
ex.zh: 「heavy rain」是英文中常見的搭配詞。

ex.en: Learning collocations helps your writing sound more natural.
ex.zh: 學習詞語搭配能讓你的寫作更自然。

ex.en: It was purely coincidental that we chose the same dress.
ex.zh: 我們挑了同一件洋裝純屬巧合。

ex.en: Any similarity to real people is coincidental.
ex.zh: 與真實人物如有雷同，純屬巧合。

ex.en: The collie guided the sheep back to the barn.
ex.zh: 柯利牧羊犬把羊群趕回了穀倉。

ex.en: Our neighbor has a gentle collie with a long coat.
ex.zh: 我們的鄰居養了一隻毛很長、性情溫和的柯利牧羊犬。

ex.en: This book is a compendium of useful travel tips.
ex.zh: 這本書是實用旅遊小秘訣的彙編。

ex.en: She wrote a compendium of local recipes for the village.
ex.zh: 她替村子編了一本當地食譜的彙編。

ex.en: The two teams worked cooperatively to finish the project.
ex.zh: 兩個團隊合作完成了這個專案。

ex.en: Children learn to play cooperatively at a young age.
ex.zh: 孩子很小就學會與人合作玩耍。

ex.en: We met at a quiet coffeehouse near the station.
ex.zh: 我們在車站附近一間安靜的咖啡館碰面。

ex.en: Writers once gathered in the coffeehouse to share ideas.
ex.zh: 作家們過去常聚集在咖啡館裡交流想法。

ex.en: The movie has a convoluted plot that is hard to follow.
ex.zh: 這部電影劇情錯綜複雜，很難跟上。

ex.en: He gave a convoluted explanation that confused everyone.
ex.zh: 他的解釋繞來繞去，讓大家更困惑。

compromised.zh: 妥協、讓步（compromise 的過去式）

ex.en: Both sides compromised and signed the deal.
ex.zh: 雙方各退一步並簽下協議。

ex.en: We compromised on a price that suited us both.
ex.zh: 我們在雙方都能接受的價格上達成妥協。

ex.en: The leaked file compromised the company's security.
ex.zh: 外洩的檔案危及了公司的安全。

ex.en: His honesty was compromised by that lie.
ex.zh: 那個謊言損害了他的誠信。

ex.en: Soldiers commandeered the trucks to move supplies.
ex.zh: 士兵徵用了卡車來運送物資。

ex.en: Someone commandeered my chair while I was away.
ex.zh: 我不在的時候有人把我的椅子佔走了。

ex.en: Doves coo softly in the morning.
ex.zh: 鴿子在早晨輕輕地咕咕叫。

ex.en: She cooed to the baby until he fell asleep.
ex.zh: 她輕聲對寶寶說話，直到他睡著。

ex.en: The movie's ending felt contrived and hard to believe.
ex.zh: 這部電影的結局顯得牽強，很難讓人相信。

ex.en: Their meeting seemed contrived, as if someone had planned it.
ex.zh: 他們的相遇看起來很刻意，彷彿有人安排好的。

ex.en: The two companies are cooperating on a new project.
ex.zh: 那兩家公司正在合作一個新專案。

ex.en: Thank you for cooperating with the police.
ex.zh: 謝謝你配合警方。

ex.en: The concealment of the facts made people angry.
ex.zh: 隱瞞事實讓大家很生氣。

ex.en: The thief searched for a place of concealment.
ex.zh: 小偷尋找一個藏身的地方。

ex.en: Wash your hands to prevent the spread of contagion.
ex.zh: 勤洗手以防止傳染擴散。

ex.en: The school was closed for fear of contagion.
ex.zh: 學校因為擔心傳染而停課。

ex.en: Investors feared a financial contagion across the region.
ex.zh: 投資人擔心金融風暴會蔓延到整個地區。

ex.en: Panic can spread like a contagion in a crowd.
ex.zh: 恐慌在人群中會像傳染病一樣蔓延。

ex.en: The 1960s counterculture challenged traditional values.
ex.zh: 1960 年代的反主流文化挑戰了傳統價值觀。

ex.en: The band became a symbol of the youth counterculture.
ex.zh: 這個樂團成了青年反主流文化的象徵。

ex.en: She conscientiously checked every detail of the report.
ex.zh: 她認真地檢查了報告的每個細節。

ex.en: He conscientiously cared for his sick mother.
ex.zh: 他盡心盡力照顧生病的母親。

ex.en: There is little congruence between what he says and what he does.
ex.zh: 他說的和做的很不一致。

ex.en: The congruence of the two triangles can be proved easily.
ex.zh: 這兩個三角形的全等很容易證明。

ex.en: We are cognizant of the risks involved.
ex.zh: 我們很清楚其中涉及的風險。

ex.en: The manager was not cognizant of the problem.
ex.zh: 經理並沒有察覺到這個問題。

ex.en: Do you have a corkscrew to open this wine?
ex.zh: 你有開瓶器可以開這瓶酒嗎？

ex.en: He pulled the cork out with a corkscrew.
ex.zh: 他用開瓶器把軟木塞拔出來。

constituted.zh: 構成；組成（constitute 的過去式與過去分詞）

ex.en: Women constituted more than half of the audience.
ex.zh: 女性占了觀眾的一半以上。

ex.en: Taken together, these small changes constituted a major improvement.
ex.zh: 這些小改變合在一起，就構成了很大的進步。

ex.en: Her parents coddled her, so she never learned to cook.
ex.zh: 她的父母很寵她，所以她一直沒學會做飯。

ex.en: You shouldn't coddle your players; they need to learn to work hard.
ex.zh: 你不該太寵球員，他們需要學會努力。

contained.zh: 包含；含有（contain 的過去式）

ex.en: The box contained old photos and letters.
ex.zh: 盒子裡裝著舊照片和信件。

ex.en: The report contained several mistakes.
ex.zh: 這份報告含有好幾個錯誤。

contained.zh: 控制住；遏制（contain 的過去式）

ex.en: Firefighters contained the fire before it reached the houses.
ex.zh: 消防員在火勢蔓延到住家之前就把火控制住了。

ex.en: She barely contained her excitement during the ceremony.
ex.zh: 典禮進行時，她幾乎壓不住心中的興奮。

ex.en: The colonizers took control of the island in the 1600s.
ex.zh: 殖民者在十七世紀控制了這座島。

ex.en: History books describe the colonizer's impact on local people.
ex.zh: 歷史書描述了殖民者對當地人民的影響。

ex.en: The bird's bright coloration helps attract a mate.
ex.zh: 這種鳥鮮豔的色彩有助於吸引配偶。

ex.en: The coloration of the leaves changes in autumn.
ex.zh: 葉子的顏色在秋天會改變。

ex.en: Try to respond to criticism constructively.
ex.zh: 試著用建設性的態度回應批評。

ex.en: They discussed the problem constructively and found a solution.
ex.zh: 他們建設性地討論問題，找到了解決辦法。

ex.en: The driver was comatose for three days after the accident.
ex.zh: 那位駕駛在事故後昏迷了三天。

ex.en: Doctors are watching the comatose patient closely.
ex.zh: 醫生正密切觀察那位昏迷的病人。

ex.en: He covertly checked his phone during the meeting.
ex.zh: 他在會議中偷偷看了手機。

ex.en: The two countries covertly shared information for years.
ex.zh: 這兩國多年來暗中分享情報。

ex.en: The crane uses a heavy counterweight to stay balanced.
ex.zh: 起重機用一個很重的配重來保持平衡。

ex.en: Small shops act as a counterweight to big chains.
ex.zh: 小店可以制衡大型連鎖店。

ex.en: She is good at communicating her ideas clearly.
ex.zh: 她很擅長清楚地表達自己的想法。

ex.en: We are communicating by email while he travels.
ex.zh: 他旅行期間我們用電子郵件保持聯絡。

ex.en: The bakery sells a sweet confection of chocolate and nuts.
ex.zh: 這間烘焙坊賣一種用巧克力和堅果做的甜點。

ex.en: The cake was a beautiful confection decorated with flowers.
ex.zh: 這個蛋糕是一件用花朵裝飾的精美甜點。

ex.en: He lowered his voice in a conspiratorial whisper.
ex.zh: 他壓低聲音，神祕兮兮地低語。

ex.en: They shared a conspiratorial smile across the table.
ex.zh: 他們隔著桌子交換了心照不宣的微笑。

ex.en: She is conversant with several computer languages.
ex.zh: 她熟悉好幾種電腦語言。

ex.en: Are you conversant with the rules of this game?
ex.zh: 你熟悉這個遊戲的規則嗎？

ex.en: The army was conquering one city after another.
ex.zh: 軍隊一座接一座地攻下城市。

ex.en: She is conquering her fear of public speaking.
ex.zh: 她正在克服對公開演講的恐懼。

ex.en: The office has a friendly, collegial atmosphere.
ex.zh: 這間辦公室有友善、融洽的同事氣氛。

ex.en: She is known for her collegial way of working.
ex.zh: 她以與同事合作融洽的工作方式聞名。

ex.en: Salt water can corrode metal quickly.
ex.zh: 海水會很快腐蝕金屬。

ex.en: The old pipes began to corrode and leak.
ex.zh: 舊水管開始腐蝕並漏水。

ex.en: People often conflate fame with success.
ex.zh: 人們常常把名氣和成功混為一談。

ex.en: Don't conflate these two different problems.
ex.zh: 不要把這兩個不同的問題混為一談。

ex.en: The teacher scolded the copycat who copied her answers.
ex.zh: 老師責罵那個抄她答案的模仿者。

ex.en: A copycat crime followed the famous case.
ex.zh: 那起著名案件之後出現了模仿犯罪。

ex.en: The cosmologist studies how the universe began.
ex.zh: 那位宇宙學家研究宇宙如何誕生。

ex.en: A cosmologist spoke at the science festival.
ex.zh: 一位宇宙學家在科學節上演講。

ex.en: I spend two hours a day commuting to work.
ex.zh: 我每天花兩個小時通勤上班。

ex.en: Commuting by bike has made me much healthier.
ex.zh: 騎車通勤讓我健康多了。

ex.en: Age was included as a covariate in the analysis.
ex.zh: 分析中把年齡列為共變數。

ex.en: The researcher checked each covariate before drawing a conclusion.
ex.zh: 研究者在下結論前檢查了每個共變數。

conservator.zh: （文物的）修復保存人員；保管人

ex.en: A conservator carefully cleaned the old painting.
ex.zh: 一位文物修復師小心地清理那幅舊畫。

ex.en: The museum hired a conservator to protect its fragile books.
ex.zh: 博物館聘請了一位保存人員來保護脆弱的書籍。

ex.en: It sounds counterintuitive, but resting can make you stronger.
ex.zh: 聽起來違反直覺，但休息反而能讓你更強壯。

ex.en: The result was counterintuitive and surprised the researchers.
ex.zh: 這個結果違反直覺，讓研究人員很意外。

ex.en: Confetti fell from the ceiling at midnight.
ex.zh: 午夜時，彩色紙屑從天花板灑落。

ex.en: The guests threw confetti as the couple left the church.
ex.zh: 新人離開教堂時，賓客們拋灑彩色紙屑。

ex.en: The shop prices its goods competitively.
ex.zh: 這家店的商品定價很有競爭力。

ex.en: The two brothers play chess competitively.
ex.zh: 這對兄弟下棋時互相較勁。

ex.en: She spoke to him with obvious condescension.
ex.zh: 她用明顯高高在上的態度跟他說話。

ex.en: I hate the condescension in his voice.
ex.zh: 我討厭他聲音中那種居高臨下的口氣。

ex.en: "And" and "but" are common connectives in English.
ex.zh: and 和 but 是英文中常見的連接詞。

ex.en: Use a connective to link the two sentences.
ex.zh: 用一個連接詞把這兩個句子連起來。

ex.en: Connective tissue holds the body's parts together.
ex.zh: 結締組織把身體的各部分連在一起。

ex.en: The writer added connective phrases to improve the flow.
ex.zh: 作者加了一些連接用語讓文章更流暢。

ex.en: The two studies reached convergent results.
ex.zh: 這兩項研究得出趨於一致的結果。

ex.en: The lines on the map are convergent near the city.
ex.zh: 地圖上的這些線在城市附近交會。

ex.en: A huge conflagration destroyed the old warehouse district.
ex.zh: 一場大火燒毀了舊倉庫區。

ex.en: Firefighters struggled to control the conflagration in the forest.
ex.zh: 消防員奮力控制森林裡的大火。

ex.en: The commandant inspected the troops at the military academy.
ex.zh: 司令官視察了軍校的部隊。

ex.en: The new commandant gave a short speech to the cadets.
ex.zh: 新任指揮官對學員發表了簡短的談話。

ex.en: He sells old toys and other collectibles online.
ex.zh: 他在網路上賣舊玩具和其他收藏品。

ex.en: The shop is full of rare collectibles from the 1960s.
ex.zh: 那家店擺滿了六〇年代的珍稀收藏品。

ex.en: Many people complain about the commercialism of the holiday season.
ex.zh: 許多人抱怨節慶季節太過商業化。

ex.en: The artist rejected commercialism and refused to sell out.
ex.zh: 那位藝術家拒絕商業主義，不肯為錢妥協。

ex.en: She is coordinating the school trip for 100 students.
ex.zh: 她正在統籌一百名學生的校外旅行。

ex.en: Coordinating everyone's schedules takes a lot of time.
ex.zh: 協調每個人的時間表要花很多時間。

ex.en: Some people love coriander, but others think it tastes like soap.
ex.zh: 有些人愛香菜，也有人覺得它吃起來像肥皂。

ex.en: Sprinkle fresh coriander on the soup before serving.
ex.zh: 上桌前在湯上撒些新鮮香菜。

ex.en: The cat purred contentedly on her lap.
ex.zh: 貓咪在她腿上滿足地呼嚕著。

ex.en: He sat back and sipped his tea contentedly.
ex.zh: 他往後靠著，心滿意足地啜著茶。

ex.en: The doctor treated him for congestive heart failure.
ex.zh: 醫生為他治療充血性心臟衰竭。

ex.en: Congestive symptoms include a blocked nose and a heavy chest.
ex.zh: 充血症狀包括鼻塞和胸悶。

ex.en: Police set up a cordon around the area.
ex.zh: 警方在該區域周圍設置了封鎖線。

ex.en: Reporters were kept behind the cordon.
ex.zh: 記者被擋在警戒線後面。

ex.en: Officers cordoned off the street after the accident.
ex.zh: 事故發生後，警員封鎖了街道。

ex.en: The area was cordoned off for safety.
ex.zh: 為了安全，這個區域被圍了起來。

ex.en: She is copying notes from the board.
ex.zh: 她正從黑板上抄筆記。

ex.en: Copying someone else's homework is cheating.
ex.zh: 抄別人的作業是作弊。

ex.en: The office charges ten cents for copying.
ex.zh: 辦公室影印一張收十分錢。

ex.en: Copying this software without permission is illegal.
ex.zh: 未經許可複製這套軟體是違法的。

cogent.zh: 有說服力的；令人信服的

ex.en: She made a cogent argument for starting the project earlier.
ex.zh: 她提出了有說服力的論點，主張提早開始這個專案。

ex.en: The lawyer gave a cogent explanation that the whole jury understood.
ex.zh: 律師的解釋十分中肯，全體陪審員都聽懂了。

ex.en: I found his reasons cogent, so I changed my mind.
ex.zh: 我覺得他的理由很有說服力，所以改變了想法。

ex.en: The shop sells chocolates and other confectionery.
ex.zh: 這家店賣巧克力和其他糖果點心。

ex.en: She works in a confectionery factory near the station.
ex.zh: 她在車站附近的糖果工廠工作。

ex.en: Stress raises the level of cortisol in the body.
ex.zh: 壓力會提高體內的皮質醇濃度。

ex.en: Good sleep helps keep cortisol under control.
ex.zh: 良好的睡眠有助於控制皮質醇。

ex.en: The earthquake began to convulse the whole region.
ex.zh: 地震開始讓整個地區劇烈震動。

ex.en: The joke made the audience convulse with laughter.
ex.zh: 那個笑話讓觀眾笑得前仰後合。

ex.en: The cornea is the clear front part of the eye.
ex.zh: 角膜是眼睛前方透明的部分。

ex.en: He had surgery to repair a scratch on his cornea.
ex.zh: 他動手術修復角膜上的刮傷。

ex.en: She told her confessor about her worries.
ex.zh: 她把自己的煩惱告訴了聽她告解的神父。

ex.en: The priest served as a confessor to many families in the town.
ex.zh: 這位神父是鎮上許多家庭的告解神父。

constructed.zh: 建造；構成（construct 的過去式與過去分詞）

ex.en: The workers constructed a small bridge over the stream.
ex.zh: 工人在小溪上建了一座小橋。

ex.en: The house was constructed entirely of wood.
ex.zh: 這棟房子完全是用木頭建造的。

complicating.zh: 使複雜化（complicate 的現在分詞）

ex.en: You are complicating a very simple problem.
ex.zh: 你把一個很簡單的問題複雜化了。

ex.en: Heavy rain kept complicating our travel plans.
ex.zh: 大雨不斷讓我們的旅行計畫變得更複雜。

ex.en: The clerk courteously answered all our questions.
ex.zh: 店員有禮貌地回答了我們所有的問題。

ex.en: He bowed courteously and held the door open.
ex.zh: 他客氣地鞠躬並替我們扶著門。

ex.en: The company took new countermeasures against online fraud.
ex.zh: 公司針對網路詐騙採取了新的對策。

ex.en: Wearing a helmet is a simple countermeasure that reduces injuries.
ex.zh: 戴安全帽是減少傷害的簡單對策。

ex.en: Pigeons sat along the cornice of the old building.
ex.zh: 鴿子停在老建築的簷口上。

ex.en: The workers painted the decorative cornice white.
ex.zh: 工人把裝飾用的簷口漆成白色。

ex.en: Students are compulsorily vaccinated before entering this school.
ex.zh: 學生入學前必須強制接種疫苗。

ex.en: The land was compulsorily purchased to build a new road.
ex.zh: 那塊土地被強制徵收來興建新道路。

ex.en: The actor has great comedic timing.
ex.zh: 這位演員有絕佳的喜劇節奏感。

ex.en: She wrote a comedic story about a clumsy waiter.
ex.zh: 她寫了一個關於笨手笨腳服務生的喜劇故事。

ex.en: The test found coliform in the well water.
ex.zh: 檢測在井水中發現了大腸菌群。

ex.en: High coliform levels mean the water may be unsafe.
ex.zh: 大腸菌群數值偏高代表水可能不安全。

ex.en: The tiny room felt confining after a week indoors.
ex.zh: 在室內待了一週後，那間小房間讓人覺得很侷促。

ex.en: He found the strict rules too confining.
ex.zh: 他覺得那些嚴格的規定太拘束了。

ex.en: We spent a convivial evening with old friends.
ex.zh: 我們和老朋友度過了歡樂的夜晚。

ex.en: The café has a warm and convivial atmosphere.
ex.zh: 這間咖啡館的氣氛溫暖又愉快。

ex.en: A concave lens makes objects look smaller.
ex.zh: 凹透鏡會讓物體看起來比較小。

ex.en: The spoon has a concave shape.
ex.zh: 這支湯匙是凹形的。

ex.en: The puppy tripped comically over its own ears.
ex.zh: 小狗滑稽地被自己的耳朵絆倒。

ex.en: He comically pretended to faint when he saw the bill.
ex.zh: 他看到帳單時滑稽地假裝昏倒。

ex.en: The local constabulary investigated the break-in.
ex.zh: 當地警察隊調查了這起闖空門案件。

ex.en: The constabulary asked residents for information.
ex.zh: 警方向居民徵求相關消息。

ex.en: She was her sister's closest confidante.
ex.zh: 她是姊姊最親近的知己。

ex.en: The queen trusted her confidante with every secret.
ex.zh: 女王把所有秘密都託付給她的知己。

ex.en: The little boy kept coughing all night.
ex.zh: 那個小男孩整晚不停咳嗽。

ex.en: Stop coughing and drink some warm water.
ex.zh: 別再咳了，喝點溫水吧。

ex.en: The fire was small and easily controllable.
ex.zh: 火勢不大，很容易控制。

ex.en: Some risks are not controllable, so we need a backup plan.
ex.zh: 有些風險無法控制，所以我們需要備案。

ex.en: The test checks how children are developing cognitively.
ex.zh: 這項測驗檢查孩子在認知方面的發展。

ex.en: Reading every day keeps older people cognitively active.
ex.zh: 每天閱讀能讓長者的認知保持活躍。

ex.en: I eat a bowl of cornflakes with milk every morning.
ex.zh: 我每天早上都吃一碗加牛奶的玉米片。

ex.en: Crushed cornflakes make a crunchy coating for chicken.
ex.zh: 把玉米片壓碎可以給炸雞裹上酥脆的外皮。

ex.en: She held the conch shell up to her ear to hear the sea.
ex.zh: 她把海螺殼貼近耳朵，想聽見海浪聲。

ex.en: They blew a conch to call everyone to the beach.
ex.zh: 他們吹響海螺，召喚大家到海灘集合。

ex.en: This is a correlational study, so it cannot prove cause and effect.
ex.zh: 這是一項相關性研究，所以不能證明因果關係。

ex.en: The team ran a correlational analysis of sleep and test scores.
ex.zh: 研究團隊對睡眠與考試成績做了相關性分析。

ex.en: The two companies were accused of colluding to raise prices.
ex.zh: 這兩家公司被指控串通哄抬價格。

ex.en: Officials should never collude with criminals.
ex.zh: 官員絕不該與罪犯勾結。

ex.en: The doctor ordered a confirmatory test to be sure of the result.
ex.zh: 醫生安排了一項確認性檢驗，以確定結果。

ex.en: We need confirmatory evidence before we can accept this claim.
ex.zh: 我們需要有證實的證據，才能接受這項說法。

cooled.zh: 使冷卻；變涼（cool 的過去式與過去分詞）

ex.en: We let the soup cool, and by then it had cooled enough to eat.
ex.zh: 我們讓湯放涼，到那時它已涼到可以喝了。

ex.en: The evening breeze cooled the hot streets.
ex.zh: 傍晚的微風使炙熱的街道涼了下來。

ex.en: After the argument, they cooled down and talked calmly.
ex.zh: 爭吵之後，他們冷靜下來，平心靜氣地談話。

ex.en: Pour the cooled tea over the ice.
ex.zh: 把放涼的茶倒在冰塊上。

ex.en: The cooled engine can be touched safely.
ex.zh: 冷卻後的引擎可以安全觸摸。

ex.en: We had chili with a slice of warm cornbread.
ex.zh: 我們吃了辣豆醬，配一片溫熱的玉米麵包。

ex.en: Grandma bakes cornbread in a heavy iron pan.
ex.zh: 奶奶用一個厚重的鐵鍋烤玉米麵包。

ex.en: She told me confidentially that she planned to quit.
ex.zh: 她私下告訴我她打算辭職。

ex.en: All patient records are handled confidentially.
ex.zh: 所有病患的紀錄都會保密處理。

ex.en: The new nurse handled the emergency competently.
ex.zh: 新來的護理師稱職地處理了這次緊急狀況。

ex.en: She competently managed the project from start to finish.
ex.zh: 她從頭到尾能幹地管理這個專案。

ex.en: My doctor advised me to have a colonoscopy at fifty.
ex.zh: 醫師建議我五十歲時做結腸鏡檢查。

ex.en: You must follow a special diet before a colonoscopy.
ex.zh: 做結腸鏡檢查前必須遵照特殊飲食。

ex.en: The program computed the final score in a few seconds.
ex.zh: 程式在幾秒鐘內算出了最終分數。

ex.en: She computed the cost of the trip and found it too high.
ex.zh: 她算了旅行的費用，發現太高了。

ex.en: Confucian ideas about respect for elders remain influential.
ex.zh: 儒家敬老的思想至今仍有影響力。

ex.en: She studied Confucian philosophy at university.
ex.zh: 她在大學研讀儒家哲學。

ex.en: The story is about a ghost that takes on a corporeal form.
ex.zh: 這個故事講的是一隻幽靈變成有形的身體。

ex.en: Hunger and thirst are corporeal needs.
ex.zh: 飢餓與口渴是身體的需求。

ex.en: The tax cut had a countervailing effect on rising prices.
ex.zh: 減稅對上漲的物價產生了抵消作用。

ex.en: There was no countervailing force to stop the change.
ex.zh: 沒有任何對抗的力量能阻止這項改變。

ex.en: Each congregant received a candle at the service.
ex.zh: 每位會眾在禮拜中都領到一支蠟燭。

ex.en: The pastor greeted every congregant at the door.
ex.zh: 牧師在門口迎接每一位會眾。

ex.en: She felt a constriction in her chest when she ran.
ex.zh: 她跑步時感到胸口一陣緊縮。

ex.en: Cold weather can cause the constriction of blood vessels.
ex.zh: 寒冷的天氣會造成血管收縮。

collectible.zh: 可收集的；有收藏價值的

ex.en: These old toys are very collectible now.
ex.zh: 這些舊玩具現在很有收藏價值。

ex.en: He keeps a shelf of collectible stamps.
ex.zh: 他有一個架子擺滿了有收藏價值的郵票。

ex.en: The shop sells rare comic books and other collectibles.
ex.zh: 這間店賣稀有漫畫和其他收藏品。

ex.en: Her grandfather's watch became a valuable collectible.
ex.zh: 她祖父的手錶成了很有價值的收藏品。

ex.en: A huge colossus once stood at the harbor entrance.
ex.zh: 一座巨大的雕像曾矗立在港口入口。

ex.en: The company grew into a colossus in the tech industry.
ex.zh: 這家公司成長為科技業的龐然大物。

ex.en: The Congolese music was lively and full of rhythm.
ex.zh: 那首剛果音樂活潑又充滿節奏感。

ex.en: She tried a traditional Congolese dish at the festival.
ex.zh: 她在慶典上嘗了一道傳統剛果菜餚。

ex.en: Many Congolese live in the capital city.
ex.zh: 許多剛果人住在首都。

ex.en: A Congolese told us about life in his village.
ex.zh: 一位剛果人向我們談起他村裡的生活。

ex.en: We bought a new set of cookware for our kitchen.
ex.zh: 我們為廚房買了一組新的炊具。

ex.en: Non-stick cookware is easy to clean after dinner.
ex.zh: 不沾鍋的炊具在晚餐後很好清洗。

ex.en: The piece ends with a quiet coda on the piano.
ex.zh: 這首曲子以鋼琴演奏的安靜結尾段作結。

ex.en: The composer added a short coda to the final movement.
ex.zh: 作曲家在最後樂章加了一小段結尾。

ex.en: The scene at the airport was a sad coda to their story.
ex.zh: 機場那一幕是他們故事裡悲傷的尾聲。

ex.en: She added a coda to her speech, thanking everyone again.
ex.zh: 她在演講最後加了一段結語，再次感謝大家。

ex.en: The doctor explained how a cochlear implant helps people hear.
ex.zh: 醫生解釋了人工耳蝸如何幫助人聽見聲音。

ex.en: The cochlear nerve carries sound signals to the brain.
ex.zh: 耳蝸神經把聲音訊號傳到大腦。

ex.en: The officials connived with the smugglers to hide the goods.
ex.zh: 官員與走私者串通，把貨物藏起來。

ex.en: She refused to connive in the cheating.
ex.zh: 她拒絕默許這種作弊行為。

ex.en: Pour the pasta into a colander to drain the water.
ex.zh: 把義大利麵倒進濾盆裡瀝乾水。

ex.en: She washed the grapes in a colander.
ex.zh: 她用瀝水籃清洗葡萄。

ex.en: The commissioned artist painted a large mural on the wall.
ex.zh: 受委託的藝術家在牆上畫了一幅大型壁畫。

ex.en: He became a commissioned officer after finishing training.
ex.zh: 完成訓練後，他成為一名受任官階的軍官。

conquered.zh: 征服；克服（conquer 的過去式／過去分詞）

ex.en: The army conquered the city after a long siege.
ex.zh: 軍隊在長期圍城後攻下了那座城市。

ex.en: She finally conquered her fear of flying.
ex.zh: 她終於克服了對搭飛機的恐懼。

ex.en: He bowed his head in contrition after breaking his promise.
ex.zh: 他違背承諾後，懊悔地低下了頭。

ex.en: She wrote a letter full of contrition to apologize.
ex.zh: 她寫了一封充滿悔意的信來道歉。

ex.en: Video conferencing lets us meet without traveling.
ex.zh: 視訊會議讓我們不必出差就能開會。

ex.en: The office installed new conferencing equipment last month.
ex.zh: 辦公室上個月裝了新的會議設備。

conflicted.zh: 抵觸；衝突（conflict 的過去式、過去分詞）

ex.en: The meeting conflicted with my doctor's appointment.
ex.zh: 那場會議和我的看診時間衝突了。

ex.en: Their opinions conflicted, so the debate went on.
ex.zh: 他們的意見相左，所以辯論持續下去。

courting.zh: 追求；招致（court 的現在分詞）

ex.en: He has been courting her for almost a year.
ex.zh: 他追求她將近一年了。

ex.en: Speeding all the time is courting disaster.
ex.zh: 老是超速等於是在自招災禍。

ex.en: The soldiers shared a deep sense of comradeship.
ex.zh: 士兵們之間有著深厚的同袍情誼。

ex.en: Team sports build comradeship among students.
ex.zh: 團體運動能增進學生之間的夥伴情誼。

consuming.zh: 消耗；吃喝（consume 的現在分詞）

ex.en: The old heater is consuming a lot of electricity.
ex.zh: 那台舊暖氣機耗了很多電。

ex.en: He kept consuming snacks while watching the game.
ex.zh: 他看比賽時一直在吃零食。

consuming.zh: 占據全部心思的；耗時的

ex.en: Her consuming passion for music filled her days.
ex.zh: 她對音樂的狂熱占據了她所有的日子。

ex.en: Filling out the forms was a time-consuming task.
ex.zh: 填寫這些表格是件很耗時的事。

ex.en: We need to come up with a better plan.
ex.zh: 我們需要想出一個更好的計畫。

ex.en: She came up with a clever way to save money.
ex.zh: 她想出了一個聰明的省錢方法。

ex.en: Can anyone come up with a name for our team?
ex.zh: 有人能幫我們的團隊想個名字嗎？

come up with.en: to think of an idea, plan, or answer

ex.en: I came across my old diary while cleaning the closet.
ex.zh: 我整理衣櫃時，無意間發現了我的舊日記。

ex.en: He came across a rare book at the flea market.
ex.zh: 他在跳蚤市場偶然發現一本珍貴的書。

ex.en: If you come across Tom, tell him to call me.
ex.zh: 如果你碰巧遇到湯姆，叫他打給我。

come across.en: to find something or someone by chance

ex.en: She comes across as shy, but she's actually very funny.
ex.zh: 她給人害羞的印象，但其實非常風趣。

ex.en: His email came across as rude, even though he didn't mean it.
ex.zh: 他的郵件讀起來很無禮，雖然他不是故意的。

ex.en: You come across as confident when you speak slowly.
ex.zh: 你說話慢慢說時，給人很有自信的感覺。

come across.en: to seem to other people to have a certain quality

ex.en: You can count on me to be there on time.
ex.zh: 你可以放心，我會準時到。

ex.en: She knows she can always count on her sister.
ex.zh: 她知道自己永遠可以依靠姊姊。

ex.en: Don't count on good weather during the typhoon season.
ex.zh: 颱風季節別指望天氣會很好。

count on.en: to trust someone to do something or to be there when needed

ex.en: When will you come back from your trip?
ex.zh: 你旅行什麼時候回來？

ex.en: He came back home late last night.
ex.zh: 他昨晚很晚才回到家。

ex.en: Short skirts are coming back this year.
ex.zh: 短裙今年又開始流行了。

ex.en: The team came back to win in the last minute.
ex.zh: 這支球隊最後一分鐘反敗為勝。

come back.en: to become popular or strong again

ex.en: His name suddenly came back to me.
ex.zh: 我突然想起了他的名字。

ex.en: The details of that day slowly came back.
ex.zh: 那天的細節慢慢地回想起來了。

ex.en: She came back with a clever answer.
ex.zh: 她機智地回嘴了一句。

ex.en: He came back at the critic with a long reply.
ex.zh: 他寫了一長篇回應來反駁那位評論者。

come back.en: to answer back quickly or sharply

ex.en: Come down here and have some dinner.
ex.zh: 下來吃點晚餐吧。

ex.en: The rain came down hard all afternoon.
ex.zh: 整個下午雨都下得很大。

come down.en: to move from a higher place to a lower one

ex.en: Housing prices may come down next year.
ex.zh: 明年房價可能會下跌。

ex.en: The fever finally came down this morning.
ex.zh: 今天早上燒終於退了。

come down.en: to become lower in price or amount

ex.en: I think I'm coming down with a cold.
ex.zh: 我覺得我快感冒了。

ex.en: Half of the class came down with the flu.
ex.zh: 班上有一半的人得了流感。

come down.en: to start to have an illness

ex.en: This recipe has come down from my grandmother.
ex.zh: 這份食譜是從我奶奶那裡傳下來的。

ex.en: Many old songs have come down to us through the years.
ex.zh: 許多老歌這些年來一路流傳到我們這一代。

come down.en: to be passed from older people to younger ones

ex.en: Come in and sit down; the door is open.
ex.zh: 請進來坐，門沒鎖。

ex.en: The cat came in through the window.
ex.zh: 貓從窗戶進來了。

come in.en: to enter a room or building

ex.en: The train comes in at six o'clock.
ex.zh: 火車六點進站。

ex.en: News of the storm came in this morning.
ex.zh: 暴風雨的消息今天早上傳來了。

ex.en: These shoes come in three different colors.
ex.zh: 這雙鞋有三種不同的顏色。

ex.en: Does this shirt come in a larger size?
ex.zh: 這件襯衫有大一點的尺寸嗎？

come in.en: to be available in a certain form

ex.en: Long coats came in again this winter.
ex.zh: 長大衣今年冬天又流行了起來。

ex.en: When did smartphones first come in?
ex.zh: 智慧型手機是什麼時候開始流行的？

ex.en: Come on, we will be late for school!
ex.zh: 快點啦，我們上學要遲到了！

ex.en: Come on, you can do it!
ex.zh: 加油，你做得到的！

come on.en: used to ask someone to hurry or try harder

ex.en: Oh, come on, you can't be serious.
ex.zh: 少來了，你不會是認真的吧。

ex.en: Come on, that is not fair at all.
ex.zh: 拜託，這一點都不公平。

come on.en: used when you do not believe someone

ex.en: The lights come on when it gets dark.
ex.zh: 天一黑燈就會亮起來。

ex.en: My favorite show comes on at eight tonight.
ex.zh: 我最愛的節目今晚八點開始。

come on.en: to start working or start being shown

ex.en: The sun finally came out after the rain.
ex.zh: 雨後太陽終於出來了。

ex.en: Come out and see the stars tonight.
ex.zh: 今晚出來看星星吧。

come out.en: to appear or leave a place

ex.en: Her new book comes out next month.
ex.zh: 她的新書下個月出版。

ex.en: When does the movie come out in Taiwan?
ex.zh: 這部電影什麼時候在台灣上映？

ex.en: The cake came out perfectly this time.
ex.zh: 這次蛋糕做得很成功。

ex.en: The red wine stain won't come out of my shirt.
ex.zh: 紅酒漬洗不掉我的襯衫。

come out.en: to end up a certain way, or to be removed by washing

ex.en: Why don't you come over for dinner on Saturday?
ex.zh: 你週六要不要過來吃晚餐？

ex.en: My friends are coming over to watch the game.
ex.zh: 我的朋友要來我家看球賽。

ex.en: A strange sleepiness came over me.
ex.zh: 我突然感到一陣奇怪的睏意。

ex.en: What has come over you today? You are so quiet.
ex.zh: 你今天是怎麼了？怎麼這麼安靜。

come over.en: to suddenly feel a strong emotion

ex.en: Your name came up in our meeting today.
ex.zh: 今天開會時有人提到你的名字。

ex.en: The question of money always comes up.
ex.zh: 錢的問題總是會被提起。

come up.en: to be mentioned or appear as a topic

ex.en: Sorry, something came up and I can't come.
ex.zh: 抱歉，臨時有事，我沒辦法去了。

ex.en: If any problems come up, please call me.
ex.zh: 如果出現任何問題，請打電話給我。

ex.en: A boy came up and asked me the time.
ex.zh: 一個男孩走過來問我現在幾點。

ex.en: The dog came up to me and wagged its tail.
ex.zh: 那隻狗走到我身邊搖尾巴。

ex.en: My birthday is coming up next week.
ex.zh: 我的生日下週就要到了。

ex.en: Exams are coming up, so I must study.
ex.zh: 考試快到了，所以我得念書。

ex.en: Let the soup cool down before you eat it.
ex.zh: 讓湯涼一下再喝。

ex.en: The engine needs time to cool down.
ex.zh: 引擎需要一些時間冷卻。

ex.en: Take a walk and cool down before you speak.
ex.zh: 先去走一走冷靜下來再說話。

ex.en: It took him an hour to cool down after the fight.
ex.zh: 吵架後他花了一個小時才冷靜下來。

cool down.en: to become calmer after being angry
